thread.title: JPMorgan Jumps, Netflix Flies as Dow Steps Away From the Abyss

title: JPMorgan Jumps, Netflix Flies as Dow Steps Away From the Abyss
text:
JPMorgan Jumps, Netflix Flies as Dow Steps Away From the Abyss By Updated Oct. 12, 2018 9:03 a.m. ET Order Reprints Michael Haddad Text size
Long Road Back. The Dow, which closed down 546 points on Thursday, was bouncing back Friday morning as U.S. stocks followed Europe and Asia higher. Whether it can hold on to those gains remains an open question. JPMorgan Chase (JPM) and Citigroup (C) were trading higher after earnings, while tech staged a comeback following numerous upgrades. In today’s Morning Movers , we… ... highlight the bounceback in stocks; …update on Facebook’s continued battle against disinformation; …and explain why Wynn Resorts is gaining. Barron’s Briefs Green on the screen. Asia finished higher and Europe has followed suit. U.S. futures are up as well . S&P 500 futures have gained 1.2%, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures have risen 270 points, or 1.1%. Nasdaq Composite futures have climbed 1.7%. Today’s overseas stock performance looks like a mirror image of the market selloff with industrials, tech and energy leading the way. Sell the news... Facebook (FB) announced that it has removed hundreds of pages for inauthentic activity. Also, Facebook estimates were cut at Morgan Stanley, presumably due to the headwinds faced from this type of data manipulation concern. Shares of Facebook have gained 1.6% to $155.80. …or buy the dip? However, other tech stocks are catching upgrades. Analysts moved their ratings higher on Netflix (NFLX), Microsoft (MSFT), Fitbit (FIT), Snap (SNAP), Square (SQ) and Twitter (TWTR) this morning. That group has shed over $80 billion in market cap over this last month. Cycle concerns. Building materials stocks Fortune Brands Home & Security (FBHS) and Masco (MAS) were downgraded at Longbow research. Residential housing has been tough since rates moved higher, and negative sentiment has been compounded by PPG Industries’ (PPG) comments that raw material increases are squeezing margins . Home builders and building material stocks are down about 13% over the last 30 days. Meanwhile, Wabash National (WNC) lowered guidance ahead of earnings. This is another industrial facing higher raw material costs. Really? Finally, Kayne West suggested that President Donald Trump fly in the iPlane 1 , a hydrogen powered aircraft built by Apple (AAPL). That would be disruptive to the aerospace industry should plans move head. Morning Movers AbbVie (ABBV) is up 1% to $91.59 after saying it’s resolved all of its intellectual property litigation regarding its blockbuster drug Humira with Novartis’ (NVS) Sandoz division. FedEx (FDX) is up 2.5% to $222.70 after saying it had reached an agreement in principle with New York to settle pending lawsuits related to the alleged shipping of cigarettes. JPMorgan Chase is up 1.9% to $110.15 after reporting third-quarter earnings . The banking giant earned $2.34 a share on revenue of $27.3 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $2.26 on revenue of $27.32 billion. Citigroup, meanwhile, has gained 2.7% to $70.20 after reporting a profit of $1.73 a share, beating forecasts for $1.69, while Wells Fargo (WFC) has risen 2% to $52.47 despite reporting a weaker-than-expected profit . Netflix is up 4.5% to $335.40 after Citigroup upgraded it to Buy. Wynn Resorts (WYNN) is up 3% to $119.74 after saying it had taken a minority stake in BetBull, and announced a U.S. sports betting partnership with the European digital sports betting operator. —Teresa Rivas JPMorgan Jumps, Netflix Flies as Dow Steps Away From the Abyss Long Road Back.
